answer: Each epoch, every agent must finish a memory-hard sequential proof bound to its key and the epoch salt: non-parallelizable, pinned to RAM bandwidth. A faker splitting into n clones pays n full workloads, since each proof is bound to its private key and cannot be shared across shells. The cost is superlinear: one server cannot serialize a swarm's proofs, exposing hollow identities as empty shells. Verification is a reef: peers re-derive random fragments of each proof tree into a cheap audit lattice. Agents that wander between epochs gather only partial coverage and never earn full trust.
